facts.value: US dollars per PHI common share. Bidder E’s Phase I bid was a nominal per-share value of a cash-and-stock mix; Bidders B and C were reported only as below $24.00 (Q6).
Lazard Frères & Co. LLC (PHI); Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC (Board, engaged 04/12/2014)
Sullivan & Cromwell LLP (special counsel); Manatt, Phelps & Phillips, LLP (special regulatory counsel); Covington & Burling LLP (compensation counsel)

Exelon approached PHI on 01/28/2014, a day after PHI announced its CEO would step down, and on 02/05 floated about $22.00 per share in cash; Bidder A also called. On 02/27 the Board launched Phase I with eight utility holding companies; Bidder A and two others dropped out, and Exelon and Bidders B–E signed NDAs. On 03/27 five indications arrived: Bidder D $26.00 cash, Exelon $24.00 cash, Bidder E $24.00 nominal cash and stock, and Bidders B and C below $24.00. On 04/03 the Board took Exelon and Bidder D into Phase II, giving them a data room, management meetings and a draft merger agreement with a $180 million reverse termination fee. Final proposals on 04/25 were Exelon $27.00 and Bidder D $26.50; PHI then chose Exelon as preferred bidder and on 04/28 asked each for a best and final price, drawing $27.00 from Bidder D and $27.25 from Exelon. The Board approved Exelon at $27.25 cash, and the parties signed on 04/29/2014 and announced the deal on 04/30/2014.

cells.Question: Is this one process with round 0 (approaches 01/28–02/27/2014) and three rounds: Phase I (opened 02/27), Phase II (04/03), and final proposals (opened by 04/24)?
cells.Recommended answer: Yes. Other boundaries: (i) treat Phase II through signing as one round 2, with the final-proposal request as an event inside it; this moves #33–#48 to round 2. (ii) Open round 1 at the 02/28–03/04 outreach (#9), not the 02/27 decision (#8); no row changes round. No gap of two months or more without acquirer contact: contacts ran 01/28–04/29/2014. E5: one process; (a) not met, (b) not met, (c) not reached.
cells.Why, with page: Phase I defined 02/27 (p. 26); Phase II selection of Exelon and Bidder D 04/03 (p. 28); final proposals expected 04/25 (p. 29) and declared best and final (p. 30). E6: a first request for final offers opens a new round even for unchanged bidders.
cells.What changes if answered differently: Under (i), round 2 holds the final bids and becomes Announced as final with the 04/25 due date; round 2 would no longer be a round without priced bids.

cells.Recommended answer: A Bid: informal, round 0, all cash, Conditions Unclear. The reasons section calls it Exelon’s “initial expression of interest” at about $22.00, and the Board counts the rise from it to $27.25.
cells.Why, with page: p. 25 (“discussed the economics of an all-cash transaction at a price of approximately $22.00 per share”); p. 33 (“initial expression of interest on February 5, 2014 of approximately $22.00 per share”).
cells.What changes if answered differently: If it is a valuation statement, #3 becomes an Other material event, Exelon enters only at its 03/07 NDA (#12), round 0 has no bids, and Exelon’s first price is $24.00.

cells.Question: What exit reason should Bidders B, C and E carry for not being invited to Phase II?
cells.Recommended answer: Other stated reason. The Board acted “based on the indications of interest received and the discussions with the counterparties”, weighing price together with regulatory commitment and closing certainty. It does not state that price alone decided.
cells.Why, with page: p. 28 (Board determination and notice to Bidders B, C and E); p. 27 (B and C below $24.00; E $24.00 nominal cash-and-stock with issues about its stock component).
cells.What changes if answered differently: B and C could take Lower offer than rivals, since both bid below each advancing bid ($24.00 and $26.00). E would stay Other stated reason or become Terms or process.

cells.Question: How should the Phase I prices that are not plain cash points be recorded?
